job: Direct manipulation of the BuildingGraph on the canvas — select and move vertices, extrude walls, place openings, assign rooms — with the form fields kept as the precise secondary input, not demoted and not removed.
wave: 8 — owns BuilderApp.tsx for this wave. Nothing else may touch it.
context: Surveyed before writing. Every identifier below was read out of the source, including the ones that do NOT exist.

THERE IS ZERO DRAG INTERACTION ON THE 3D CANVAS TODAY. Viewport.tsx has exactly one pointer affordance: an onClick with e.stopPropagation() on the VolumeGroup <group> at :345. SurfacePicker.tsx is the only raycasting code (its own THREE.Raycaster at :112, a DOM pointerdown listener at :159, CLICK_SLOP_PX = 4) and it raycasts houseRef only. You are building the interaction from nothing.

YOU CAN AVOID TOUCHING Viewport.tsx ENTIRELY. It already accepts houseChildren?: ReactNode (Viewport.tsx:782-784), mounted INSIDE the export-root <group ref={houseRef}>, and it currently carries FixtureLayer. That prop was built for exactly this. Use it. This is what keeps PR01 from colliding with VW02 and VW03, both of which edit Viewport.tsx.

THE PATTERN TO COPY IS Plan2D.tsx, not GraphPlanEditor.tsx. Plan2D has the full drag grammar — type Drag = pan | volume | wall | corner | opening | opening-end | partition | partition-end | partition-door | draw (:170-180), DragState { drag, spec0, parts0, label, moved } (:182), Preview { spec, partitions, adjusted, readout, guides, draft } (:192) — and it commits ONCE on pointerup with Escape emitting nothing. But it operates on HomeSpec, not BuildingGraph.

GraphPlanEditor.tsx is the graph-aware editor and it is SVG, not canvas. It commits once on release: finishDrag calls onEdit(candidate, `graph:vertex:${id}`) at :117, snap hardcoded 0.5 ft at :103. Its props are { graph, onEdit(graph, label) } (:56-62). Read it for the label grammar; do not duplicate its UI.

MUTATORS THAT EXIST (lib/builder/buildingGraph.ts, all pure, all validate-then-swap): moveGraphVertex(graph, storeyId, vertexId, point, snapFt=0) :731 · splitWallAt(graph, storeyId, wallId, distanceFromStartFt, vertexId) :766 · addPartitionEdge(...) :865 · addGraphOpening(graph, storeyId, wallId, opening) :914 · duplicateGraphStorey :938 · setGraphStoreyLevels :1002 · addGraphStair :1034 · addGraphShaft :1108 · deriveRoomFaces :304 · validateBuildingGraph :445.

MUTATORS THAT DO NOT EXIST: deleteGraphVertex, deleteWall, moveWall, extrudeWall, renameRoom, moveGraphOpening. The graph row's 'extrude walls' and 'assign rooms' therefore need NET-NEW pure mutators in buildingGraph.ts, or must compose splitWallAt + moveGraphVertex. Decide which, and say which.

TYPE TRAPS THAT WILL COST YOU: GraphMutation's FAILURE branch carries `graph` ({ ok:false; problem; graph }, :138) while BuildingGraphValidation's (:134) and GraphFactoryResult's (:142) do not. GraphRoomFace.areaSqft has a lowercase f — unlike footprintSqFt and totalFloorAreaSqFt everywhere else. Do not cross-pollinate the many different `status` unions in this repo (document.ts:89 is 'modelled'|'proxy'; projectBudget.ts:49 is 'modelled'|'allowance'|'quote-needed'; readiness.ts:33 is 'design-intent'|'review-ready').

The reducer action you dispatch is { type: 'graph'; graph: BuildingGraph; label: string } (BuilderApp.tsx:250-260), via editGraph(next, label) at :750. HISTORY_MAX = 80 (:264); history coalesces on `label`, so a drag emitting one label per frame would eat the undo stack.
The hash for the gate: hashBuilderDocument(document): Hex at lib/builder/document.ts:571 (keccak256 over canonicalBuilderDocumentJson, :565, which throws if validation fails).
doNotTouch: app/components/builder/Viewport.tsx — enter through the existing houseChildren prop. If you believe you genuinely cannot, STOP and report rather than reaching; VW02 and VW03 own that file in neighbouring waves and a shared-tree collision there is silent data loss, not a merge conflict.
app/components/builder/Plan2D.tsx and GraphPlanEditor.tsx — read them, copy the pattern, leave them alone.
rejectionGates: THE HEADLINE GATE: a drag and the equivalent typed edit must produce the same graph AND the same hashBuilderDocument. Assert it on at least a vertex move and one opening placement. If they differ by a float epsilon, fix the snapping — do not widen the assertion to tolerate it, because a hash that tolerates drift is not a hash.

ONE DRAG IS ONE UNDO STEP. Commit on pointerup, never per frame. Escape mid-drag must emit nothing at all — not an edit that undoes to the same place, nothing. Assert the history length before and after.

every mutation goes through the pure validate-then-swap functions in buildingGraph.ts. A canvas handle that mutates a graph object in place bypasses validateBuildingGraph and can produce a document that canonicalBuilderDocumentJson then THROWS on — which is a corrupted save, not a bad render.
the form fields stay. The founder asked for direct manipulation WITH fields as precise secondary input; a canvas that replaces the numeric inputs has removed the only way to enter an exact dimension.
the canvas must not remount and data-load-epoch must not move on a graph edit — VW01's pins.
instructions: 1. Handles live in a new GraphCanvasEditor mounted through houseChildren. Raycast against your own handle meshes, not against the house — SurfacePicker already owns house-surface picking and two raycasters fighting over one pointerdown is a bug you will not enjoy finding.
2. Preview-then-commit, exactly like Plan2D: hold a candidate graph in local state, render from it, and dispatch once on release.

3. New mutators go in buildingGraph.ts as pure functions returning GraphMutation, with the same validate-then-swap discipline as their neighbours. Extrude and room-assign are the two the graph row names; if you can compose them from existing primitives, do that and say so.
4. Where a manipulation is not honestly supported yet, no handle appears. An affordance that moves and then reverts is worse than no affordance.

5. Spec: drag ≡ typed edit ≡ same hash; one drag is one history entry; Escape emits nothing; an invalid drag (self-intersecting wall, zero-length edge) is refused by the mutator and leaves the document untouched.
